transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me?

I came in because I honestly can’t see my studio—or my life—getting back on track anymore. I work as hard as I can, and they can put whatever payment plan in front of me, but... I just don’t see how it gets better.
When did you first start feeling this way about your studio and your life—was there a specific event that triggered it, and how long has it been going on?
It started when I took on the mortgage for the studio. That was a little over two years ago—about two years and two months now.
Over these past two years, would you say your main struggle has been feeling down, empty, or losing interest in things, or has it been more about constant worry, nervousness, or feeling on edge?

It’s more feeling down. Most days I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling already on me. Even in the shop, around the wood and work I used to care about, it all feels flat. Sometimes I just have to fight not to stand there staring.
Over these past two years, has this heavy, down feeling been pretty much constant every day, or have there been stretches—weeks or months—where you actually felt like your normal self again?
I can’t really think of a stretch where I felt normal again. Most days it’s there when I wake up—that heavy, gray feeling. Even being in the shop doesn’t pull me out of it anymore.
Along with this heavy, down feeling, have you noticed changes in your sleep or appetite—like sleeping much more or less than usual, or a big change in your appetite or weight?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to my sleep or appetite, honestly.
During these past two years, have you ever had thoughts of hurting yourself or felt that life wasn't worth living?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about it in those terms.
Besides feeling down, have you noticed a drop in your energy, trouble concentrating, or feelings of worthlessness or guilt during this time?

Yeah, my energy is shot. By midmorning my arms feel like I’ve been hauling lumber all day. Even after a full night in bed, I can barely get through measuring, cutting, or returning calls without feeling wiped out.

Over these two years, has the intensity of how you're feeling stayed pretty much the same the whole time, or have there been periods where it got noticeably worse or more severe than your usual baseline?
I don’t know. It’s hard for me to tell whether it’s been worse at certain times or just… been there all along.

During this two-year period, has there ever been a stretch of at least two weeks where your mood and energy were so bad that you had real trouble just functioning—getting out of bed, running the shop, or taking care of basic responsibilities—compared to how you've been managing most of the time?

Yeah. There’ve been stretches where I just couldn’t keep up with the basic stuff. I’ve missed bids, let mortgage paperwork pile up, and lost clients who used to call me first. I’m barely holding onto the studio some days. And I stopped going to gallery openings or playing basketball—just pulled away from the things and people that mattered to me.
After that stretch when things got especially bad, did your mood and functioning ever ease back up to your usual baseline afterward, or has it stayed at that same severe level ever since?
I’m not sure. It all kind of runs together for me. I know there were times I was really struggling, but I can’t say clearly whether I got back to my normal level afterward or not.

Outside of those especially bad stretches, during your more typical day-to-day baseline over these two years, have you also struggled with concentration or feelings of worthlessness/guilt, or has it mainly just been the low mood and low energy without those other symptoms?

Yeah, I get down on myself a lot. If a joint doesn’t line up right or I miss a bid deadline, it’s not just, “I messed that up.” I start thinking I’m a lousy carpenter, like maybe I had no business trying to run my own studio in the first place.

When you're not in one of those especially bad stretches, would you say your day-to-day mood and energy are still pretty severely low, or are they noticeably milder—just a chronic 'off' feeling—compared to how bad it gets during those crisis periods?

It’s still pretty low most days. I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling already on me, and even in the shop, around the wood I used to love, everything feels flat. Sometimes I just have to fight not to stand there staring.

Over these two years, would you say you've had just one continuous stretch where things got that bad, or have there been several separate times—each followed by some return to your usual baseline—when things worsened to that level?
I honestly can’t tell. It’s hard for me to separate it into distinct periods like that. I know it’s gotten worse at times, but I don’t know whether I really came back to my usual level in between.
At any point during these two years, was there a period of at least two months where you felt essentially back to your normal self, with none of these low mood or low energy symptoms at all?
No. It’s been there since I took on the studio mortgage—so, a little over two years now, about two years and two months. I haven’t had a stretch where I felt back to normal.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a persistently low, 'heavy, gray' mood present almost continuously for over two years, without any period of at least two months of normal mood, consistent with dysthymia. Superimposed on this chronic baseline, he describes distinct stretches of more severe impairment (missed bids, withdrawal from social/recreational activities, inability to keep up with basic responsibilities) suggesting episodes meeting major depressive episode criteria embedded within the chronic low-grade depression—classic 'double depression' pattern. Core dysthymic symptoms include low energy/fatigue, self-critical thinking and guilt, anhedonia, and functional decline, with no history of manic/hypomanic symptoms and no clear-cut recurrent discrete episodes separated by full remission, favoring persistent depressive disorder over recurrent MDD.

confirmed_symptoms: Daily low, heavy, gray mood present for over two years
No period of feeling back to normal for at least two months
Anhedonia/flatness even during previously enjoyed work (woodworking)
Chronic low energy/fatigue despite adequate sleep
Self-critical thoughts and feelings of inadequacy/guilt after minor setbacks
Difficulty concentrating/functioning on tasks (measuring, cutting, calls)
Distinct stretches of worsened functioning: missed bids, paperwork piling up, lost clients
Withdrawal from valued activities (gallery openings, basketball)
Uncertain full return to baseline after these worse stretches

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms present nearly continuously for a little over two years, since taking on studio mortgage, without a period of at least two months of normal mood in between.
additional_requirements: No manic or hypomanic episodes reported
No clear-cut discrete major depressive episodes separated by full remission periods, supporting chronic persistent course over recurrent MDD
